title: Models from the catalog, not lists: what Harbour knows about a model comes from OpenRouter
description:
## As asked

Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** Harbour keeps hand-written lists of models: which ones the settings offer, which ones the free tier allows, which ones get a separate budget for hidden reasoning, and what each costs. Lists kept by hand go stale. Today they offer neither GPT-6.1 Sol nor Claude Haiku 5.5. The brief, which every step reads first, ran for weeks on `gpt-5.4-mini`, chosen in LIN-263 against models two generations old. John's sense is that a better choice exists, possibly both cheaper and better on the benchmarks that matter, and that we already have the information to see it without running evals.

On 7 November we moved the brief to Haiku 5.5. On long tickets it stopped mid-sentence at about 400 of its 3,000 tokens. The cause isn't confirmed. The reasoning-budget check reads OpenRouter's catalog first, then falls back to a list of OpenAI ids, so Haiku 5.5 was probably not flagged by the catalog. That means reading the catalog more might not be enough by itself. We moved the brief to GPT-6.1 Sol, which comes out whole.

**What we want.** In John's words, this should be automated, using data from OpenRouter, so Harbour doesn't need a list of models. That covers the facts Harbour relies on about a model: whether it reasons, what it costs, how much it can take in and put out, and whether it can use tools. A new model should work correctly on the day it appears, and a wrong guess about one should show up rather than quietly cut its output short. It also covers the choice itself. When someone picks a model for a job, Harbour should help them choose well from the data it can see, not from a curated list.

The choice stays with people: which model a job runs on, which models a workspace suggests, and what the free tier may spend on the operator's key. Where a list exists only to encode such a choice, a rule such as a price ceiling may serve better than names. Say what you'd propose, and raise a ruling where it changes what anyone may spend.

This applies to every Harbour call, not only the brief, whatever LIN-4345 decides about the brief.

**Appetite:** err larger.

**Done looks like:** any model in the catalog can run a long brief and come out whole, or Harbour says clearly why it can't. A model released tomorrow is priced, budgeted and offered correctly without anyone editing a list. The pull request says which hand lists are gone, and which remain and why.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Outcome (closed 8 Nov 2026)

Implemented in three merged PRs, all live on [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>):

* [#2362](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2362>) (`64c2ca26`): the shared call layer. Every strict call refuses a cut-off answer instead of caching it. Each call is sized from the catalog with reasoning headroom, and a `length` stop gets one bounded retry.
* [#2367](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2367>) (`bad9d719`): model facts come from the OpenRouter catalog. `MODEL_PRICING`, `REASONING_MODEL_PREFIXES`, and `AVAILABLE_MODELS` as a list of facts are gone. The lists that remain hold people's choices and are checked against the catalog. The routing call is budgeted through the same planner. Per-call recommendations are in `docs/papers/harbour/model-choice-by-call.md`.
* [#2374](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2374>) (`ab942e80`): records John's free-tier disposition in that paper.

Implemented as reviewed, with the deviations named in the close-out comments: the routing-budget witness, and the Haiku 5.5 replay deferred by John's call. Settled by John's rulings: the free tier stays on GPT-5.4 Mini behind the `FREE_TIER_MODEL_IDS` allowlist, and pickers get no benchmark column. GPT-6 Luna stays the recommendation, with evidence pending. Before any call moves to Haiku 5.5, it waits on the replay recorded in `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`.

The full history (surveys, investigation, size of the move, reviews, close-outs) is kept in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4358 @ d81e13e7d

**The diagnosis is probably aimed at the wrong layer.** `generateBrief` (`lib/brief.js:115-123`) never asks the reasoning-budget check. It sends a bare `maxTokens: 3000` with no `reasoning` field. Only the roadmap and ship-biscuit routes call `resolveReasoningBudget`. Brief, recap, session-summary, run-summary, observer-pass, scan and agent-turn all send a bare cap. If Haiku 5.5 thinks by default, its hidden tokens come out of those 3,000, and roughly 400 visible is what you'd expect. A perfect catalog flag wouldn't have saved the brief: most call sites skip the split.

**Truncation is silent where it matters.** `streamChat` reports `finishReason`, and `llm-call-log` records it along with `reasoningTokens` (LIN-3359). But `generateBrief` keeps only the text, so a cut-off brief is cached as whole. To make truncation show up, every caller has to treat `length` as an error or a retry, not just a log row. The Haiku 5.5 rows in the call log should already settle the cause, with no new code.

**The catalog reader rests on an unchecked shape.** `lib/openrouter-catalog.js` says "the live response was not read when this was written". The `reasoning.{mandatory,default_enabled}` path is a guess, and the only fixture is hand-made. `context_length` and `top_provider.max_completion_tokens` aren't kept at all, so input and output limits have nowhere to live yet.

**Why it's hard:**
- **Pricing doesn't fit the catalog cleanly.** `MODEL_PRICING` has long-context overrides, a Haiku 5.5 tier above 100k, and DeepSeek time-of-day windows. All of it is operator-pasted and checked by the hourly conformance sweep. Moving to catalog pricing means parsing `pricing.overrides`, or accepting less accurate prices.
- **Workers aren't on OpenRouter.** Claude Code reports `claude-haiku-5-5` or the alias `haiku` (`DISPATCH_CLAUDE_ALIAS_MODELS`). That mapping to catalog ids stays a hand list, or becomes a naming rule.
- **The lists are spread out:** `AVAILABLE_MODELS`, `FREE_TIER_MODEL_IDS`, `REASONING_MODEL_PREFIXES`, `DISPATCH_MODEL_SUGGESTIONS`/`REASONS`, `MODEL_PRICING`, `DEFAULT_MODEL` and the roadmap allow-list. Each behaves differently when the catalog cache is cold: some fail closed, some fail open, some fall back to the list.
- **The free tier is a spending ruling.** `FREE_TIER_MODEL_IDS` fails closed on the operator's key. A catalog price ceiling would let new models in, but then a cold or wrong catalog decides spending. That needs John's ruling, including what a cold cache does.
- **"Help them choose well" has no quality data.** The catalog covers price, context, tools and reasoning, not benchmarks. Without evals, the help is filtering and sorting, not ranking. The PR should say so plainly.

**What I'd do first:**
1. Read the Haiku 5.5 brief rows (`finishReason`, `reasoningTokens`) to confirm the cause.
2. Commit a real `/models` snapshot as a fixture, fix `normalizeModel` to match it, and keep the limit fields.
3. Route every `streamChat` caller through one budget function sized from catalog limits, and make `length` loud. That alone meets "comes out whole, or says why".
4. Then remove the lists one at a time, with the free-tier rule raised as a ruling.

## Survey global: LIN-4358 @ d81e13e7d

**Where it lands.** The model facts are spread across five places. `lib/openrouter.js` holds `DEFAULT_MODEL`, `AVAILABLE_MODELS`, `FREE_TIER_MODEL_IDS` and `REASONING_MODEL_PREFIXES`. `lib/model-pricing.js` holds `MODEL_PRICING`, rows pasted from the catalog by hand. `lib/model-routing-harnesses.js` holds `DISPATCH_MODEL_SUGGESTIONS`, `_REASONS` and `_CLAUDE_ALIAS_MODELS`. `lib/openrouter-catalog.js` is the live cache. `public/common.js` keeps a copy of the `buildModelOptions` merge. Things are improving: LIN-3882 made tools, price hints and names read the catalog first, and the cache is warmed at boot. But every catalog read is a fallback onto a list, and the same ten ids are still written out three times, pinned together by tests rather than generated.

**The ticket is aimed at a symptom.** The brief never consults the reasoning check. `lib/brief.js:122` calls `streamChat` with a bare `maxTokens: 3000`, no `reasoning`, and no handler for `done`. `resolveReasoningBudget` is opt-in per call site, and only roadmap and ship-biscuit opt in. Brief, recap, session-summary, run-summary, feedback-title, scan, agent-turn and observer-pass all send a bare cap and throw `finishReason` away. So a truncated brief goes through `composeBrief` and is cached as if whole. Also, `normalizeReasoning` reads a top-level `reasoning` object that its own comment says was never checked against a live response. If that path is wrong, the catalog half of `isReasoningModel` never fires, and only the OpenAI prefixes count as reasoning models.

**Done the obvious way** (read more catalog fields in `isReasoningModel`), all those call sites stay blind, and there are two rules: catalog facts in one place, hand-tuned per-route budgets in others. The catalog doesn't keep `context_length` or `top_provider.max_completion_tokens`, so output limits have nowhere to live yet. These would also have to change: `public/common.js`, `harnessModelsBlock()`, `public/llms.txt`, `proxy-instructions.js` examples, and the keys of `DISPATCH_MODEL_REASONS`. Only the hourly `pricing-conformance-sweep.js` (prices) and `free-tier-model.test.js` (suggestions ⊆ allowlist) would notice a missed edit.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:**
- Move budgeting into `streamChat`/`streamChatWithTools`. Callers state the prose they need. The call layer reads reasoning and max-completion from the catalog and sizes the request.
- Treat `finish_reason: 'length'` as a failure, or flag it, at the call layer. The brief must never cache a partial.
- Verify the live `/models` shape once, and pin it as a fixture.
- Price OpenRouter ids from catalog `pricing`. Keep `MODEL_PRICING` only for Claude Code worker ids the catalog can't key.
- Replace `FREE_TIER_MODEL_IDS` with a catalog price ceiling. **Ruling needed:** the ceiling, and whether an unpriced or cold-cache model fails closed. I'd say it should.

**Not this task's:** one model-facts module that the server and browser both import (`public/` has no build step). Also ranked choice on benchmarks: the catalog has no benchmark data, so that's a data-source decision.

## Size of the move (the person's call)

Err larger, John's standing answer.

Both Surveys found the cause one layer down from where the ticket put it. The brief never asks for a reasoning budget. It sends a bare 3,000-token cap, and so do most of Harbour's calls (recap, the summaries, scan, the agent turn). Only two routes use the budget check at all. A cut-off is also silent: the call log records why the output stopped, but the brief keeps only the text and caches a partial as if it were whole. So a better catalog flag alone would not have saved the brief.

So the move is larger. Confirm the cause from what was logged. Every Harbour call then gets a budget sized from what the catalog says about its model. A cut-off is loud wherever it happens, and nothing caches a partial. Every model fact the catalog holds is read from it. Any hand list that remains says why it still exists.

**The choice itself.** John's bet is that we can choose better models without running evals, from information we already have. The catalog gives prices, limits, tools and reasoning but no measure of quality. The Library has benchmark data and analysis (`docs/papers/harbour/cheaper-capacity.md` and its CSV, `docs/papers/harbour/model-choice.md`). Use them to recommend a model for each Harbour call, with the evidence and the price beside it. John makes the choice. Whether Harbour should read a quality source routinely is also his decision, so propose it rather than build it.

**The free tier.** John has said that if we find a model that's better and cheaper than today's free-tier default, he's happy to move the free tier to it. Bring that as a recommendation he can confirm: the model, why it's better on the evidence we have, the price, and every free-tier job shown working whole on it. Replacing the free-tier allowlist with a rule, such as a price ceiling, changes what may be spent on the operator's key, including what happens when the catalog is cold or a model is unpriced. Raise that as a ruling, with your recommendation.

Done includes showing that a long brief on Claude Haiku 5.5 comes out whole, without switching the brief to it.

**Order:** start after LIN-4353 lands. That ticket, the last piece of LIN-4345, is changing `lib/brief.js` now so the brief quotes the person's words word for word. Whatever LIN-4345 decides about keeping the brief, this ticket applies to every Harbour call.

**Done when** no Harbour call can quietly return a partial, every model fact the catalog holds is read from it, the hand lists that remain each say why, and John has a recommended model for each call and for the free tier, with the evidence beside it.

## Investigation: LIN-4358 @ d65d8af0

**Short version.** There are two causes, and only one of them is proven.

- **Proven:** any Harbour call except recommend, roadmap and ship-biscuit returns and caches a partial when output stops early. I reproduced this with the real `generateBrief`.
- **Not proven:** why Haiku 5.5 stopped at ~400 tokens on LIN-4352. The one log row that settles it can't be read from a worker. Below are the query and a replay script that settle it.

The fix doesn't hinge on the second answer, but one step of it does (step 2 below).

### 1. Reproduction (local, live catalog, mocked chat stream)

The harness loads the live `GET /api/v1/models` body (460 models, fetched 7 Nov 21:59 UTC) into Harbour's cache through the real `normalizeModel`. It builds the brief from the exact input Harbour snapshotted when Haiku briefed LIN-4352: snapshot `82b963e0`, 14:13:25 UTC, 33,336 chars, about 8.3k tokens. It then drives `generateBrief` through `setFetchImpl`.

- **Request Harbour sent for Haiku 5.5:** `{"model":"anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5","temperature":0,"max_tokens":3000,"stream":true,"usage":{"include":true}}`. There is no `reasoning` field and no headroom. `resolveReasoningBudget(haiku, 3000)` gives `{maxTokens:3000}`, but the brief never calls it anyway.
- **Three ways a stream can end early.** Each was replayed after ~400 visible tokens:

| Stream ended with | `generateBrief` | Call log |
|---|---|---|
| `finish_reason: 'length'`, `reasoning_tokens: 2600` | **resolves**, returns the partial | `length` / 2600 |
| mid-stream `finish_reason: 'error'` | **resolves**, returns the partial | `error` |
| no `finish_reason` (connection dropped) | **resolves**, returns the partial | `null` |

`routes/proxy-compute.js:1432` then runs `briefCacheStore.put(... inputHash ...)`. The partial is served as fresh until the ticket changes. Note also that `streamChat` clears its timeout once headers arrive (`lib/openrouter.js:1479`), so a stalled body has no deadline of its own.

**Acceptance witness.** "The brief has its four sections" is not a valid witness: a cut can land after the last heading. The valid witness is the call's own termination: `finish_reason === 'stop'` (or `tool_calls` on a tool hop), checked by the call layer. Any other value must throw or recover, and must never reach a cache.

### 2. The class: every Harbour call, by caller

None of these read `finishReason` or use the split. Each sends a bare cap:

| Caller | Cap |
|---|---|
| brief (`lib/brief.js:122`) | 3000 |
| recap (`lib/recap.js:102`) | 1500 |
| session-summary | 150 |
| run-summary | 400 |
| feedback-title | 60 |
| scan (`lib/scan.js:219` and `routes/workspace-api-scan.js:85`) | 1000 |
| observer-pass (`streamChatWithTools`) | 500 |
| agent-turn / task-chat (both paths) | turn budget |

Recap, brief, session-summary and run-summary results are all cached or stored.

Only three callers handle termination:
- **recommend:** `stage-router` reads `finishReason`, with an 8000 cap.
- **roadmap:** three call sites, using `resolveReasoningBudget` and `finishReason`.
- **ship-biscuit:** `assessEditorOutcome`.
- **Flight Companion:** `agent-turn` passes the `done` event through, and the browser shows a cut-off note (LIN-3359). This one is visible to the person, not refused.

So this is a class, not an isolated bug. Its root is that `streamChat` and `streamChatWithTools` report termination as an optional event that each caller must remember to inspect.

### 3. What the live catalog actually says (this corrects both Surveys)

**The `reasoning` path is right, but the object is not what `normalizeReasoning` assumes.**
- The live shape is `{mandatory, default_enabled?, supported_efforts, default_effort}`.
- `supports_max_tokens` does not exist, so it always normalizes to `false`.
- `default_enabled` is often **absent**: 89+77 models.
- Normalizing collapses absent to `false`, so "unknown" and "off" read the same.

| Model | Raw `reasoning` | Harbour split |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` | `{mandatory:false, default_effort:'medium'}`, no `default_enabled` | **false** |
| `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` | `{mandatory:true, default_enabled:true}` | true |
| `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` | `{mandatory:false, default_enabled:true}` | true |
| `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` | `{mandatory:false, default_enabled:false, default_effort:'medium'}` | true, **only via the OpenAI prefix list** |

**Why this matters:**
- Harbour has measured hidden reasoning eating mini's bare cap (LIN-1000, LIN-1665), yet the catalog says `default_enabled:false` for mini.
- So **the catalog's flags can't predict whether a model spends hidden tokens when not asked**. That confirms the ticket's suspicion that "reading the catalog more might not be enough by itself".
- Mini and Haiku 5.5 share `default_effort:'medium'`, which makes reasoning the leading hypothesis for Haiku. It is still a hypothesis.

**Limits are there:** `context_length` and `top_provider.max_completion_tokens` (128k for all three). Harbour discards both.

**Pricing is there, including the hard cases:**
- `pricing.overrides[]` carries `min_prompt_tokens` tiers: Haiku 5.5 is ×5 above 100k, Sol is ≥272k.
- 11 overrides carry `utc_start`/`utc_end`/`utc_days` windows (the DeepSeek case).
- All of it is parseable, so `MODEL_PRICING` is not needed for OpenRouter ids.

**Quality data is in the catalog now:** `benchmarks.artificial_analysis.{intelligence_index, coding_index, agentic_index}` on 199 of 460 models, plus `benchmarks.design_arena`. Both Surveys said the catalog had no quality data; that's no longer true.
- One discrepancy to resolve before quoting numbers: the catalog gives Haiku 5.5 **36.5** and Sol **54.6**, while the routing-log entry (from `cheaper-capacity`, 23 Oct) says 43 and 52. That's probably an index revision. The recommendation should cite one source and date it.

**Two smaller findings:**
- `temperature` is not in `supported_parameters` for Haiku 5.5, Sol or mini, yet every Harbour call sends it. It's harmless, since OpenRouter drops it, but it's another fact the catalog could gate.
- The stale lists are confirmed. `AVAILABLE_MODELS`, `FREE_TIER_MODEL_IDS` and `DISPATCH_MODEL_SUGGESTIONS` lack `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` and `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`, which `MODEL_PRICING` already has. The brief's own group default is outside the free-tier allowlist.

### 4. The decisive experiment for Haiku's stop (not run: no DB or OpenRouter key in a worker)

Rival hypotheses for "stopped mid-sentence at ~400 of 3000":
- **H1:** hidden reasoning used the cap.
- **H2:** a mid-stream provider error.
- **H3:** the stream dropped.

The "~400" in the survey log looks estimated from text length, not read from the log. One row separates the three:

```
db['llm-call-log'].find({ feature: 'brief', issueIdentifier: 'LIN-4352',
  timestamp: { $gte: ISODate('2026-11-07T14:13:00Z'), $lte: ISODate('2026-11-07T14:14:30Z') } },
  { model:1, provider:1, finishReason:1, completionTokens:1, reasoningTokens:1, maxTokens:1 })
```

How to read it:

| Row shows | Means |
|---|---|
| `length`, completion ≈3000, reasoning ≈2600 | H1 |
| `error` | H2 |
| `null` | H3 |

Alternatively, anyone with an OpenRouter key can replay the same input with snapshot `82b963e0`, `buildBriefMessages` and `streamChat` (model Haiku 5.5, `maxTokens: 3000`), then read `done.finishReason` and `usage.reasoningTokens`. The harness is in my scratchpad and can be committed as `scripts/replay-brief.mjs` by the build stage.

**Run this before building step 2's budget rule.** Steps 1 and 3 are needed under every hypothesis.

### 5. Proposed fix (at the shared call layer, reaching every caller above)

1. **Termination is part of the return value, not an optional event.**
   - `streamChat` and `streamChatWithTools` resolve to `{ text, finishReason, usage }`.
   - On anything other than `stop` (or `tool_calls` on a hop), they throw a typed `TruncatedOutputError { model, finishReason, completionTokens, reasoningTokens, maxTokens }`.
   - A caller that genuinely wants a partial (the Flight Companion cut-off note, LIN-3359) must opt in with `allowPartial: true`.
   - Routes map the error to a clear message, for example: "Haiku 5.5 spent 2,600 of 3,000 tokens reasoning; the brief was cut". Nothing reaches `briefCacheStore`, `recapCacheStore` or the session- and run-summary stores.
   - Also give the body read its own deadline.
2. **Budget sized by the call layer, from the catalog.** Callers state the visible output they need (`proseTokens`). The call layer sets `max_tokens = min(prose + reasoningAllowance, top_provider.max_completion_tokens, context_length − promptEstimate)` for any model whose catalog entry has a `reasoning` object.
   - Headroom costs nothing unless it is used. Sending a larger cap *without* a `reasoning` field avoids LIN-1665's trap (turning thinking on).
   - If a `length` still comes back with `reasoningTokens > 0`, retry once with an explicit bound: `reasoning: {max_tokens}`, or `effort: 'low'` when `supported_efforts` allows it. Log the retry, then throw.
   - Keep `default_enabled` as tri-state (`true` / `false` / `null`) in `normalizeReasoning`. Retain `supported_efforts`, `default_effort`, `context_length`, `max_completion_tokens`, `pricing.overrides` and `benchmarks.artificial_analysis`.
   - This retires `REASONING_MODEL_PREFIXES` and the per-route `resolveReasoningBudget` calls in roadmap and ship-biscuit.
3. **Fixture:** commit a trimmed real `/models` snapshot (these 5 ids plus one time-window override) as the normalizer's fixture, replacing the hand-made one.
4. **Hand lists:**
   - **Gone:** `REASONING_MODEL_PREFIXES`; `MODEL_PRICING` rows for OpenRouter ids (priced from `pricing` plus `overrides`, with the sweep re-pointed at the parser); `AVAILABLE_MODELS` (generated from the catalog, sorted and filtered by price, context, tools and AA index); and the browser's copy in `public/common.js`, which gets the same data over `/api/openrouter/models`.
   - **Remain, with reasons:** Claude Code worker ids and aliases (`haiku`, `claude-haiku-5-5`; workers are not on OpenRouter, so a naming rule or a short map stays) and their pricing; `DISPATCH_MODEL_REASONS`, if suggestions stay a human choice; and `FREE_TIER_MODEL_IDS`, until the ruling below.
5. **Witnesses for the build stage:**
   - A unit test per termination type (the three rows above) proving that each caller throws or recovers and that no cache write happens. Each must fail on today's code, which my harness already shows.
   - The live long-brief replay on Haiku 5.5 (snapshot `82b963e0`), coming out whole, without changing the brief's configured model.

### Rulings needed (John)

- **Free tier:** replace `FREE_TIER_MODEL_IDS` with a catalog price ceiling? My recommendation is yes, with these terms:
  - a ceiling on blended $/M (for example at or below today's mini rate of $0.75/$4.50);
  - **fail closed** on a cold catalog or an unpriced model, keeping today's allowlist as the cold-cache fallback;
  - every free-tier job shown whole on the candidate before the switch.

  This changes what may be spent on the operator's key, so it is not something I would decide.
- **Quality source:** the catalog's `benchmarks.artificial_analysis` is a routine quality source that costs nothing extra to read. Should Harbour show it beside price in the model picker? That's proposed, not built.

Labels: added `Bug`. Status: In Progress. Nothing was changed in code or routing; this is investigation only.

Build the call-layer fix now; settle the budget rule with the live replay at review

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

## Call-layer fix is built: PR open, CI running

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2362, head `ef36e771`. It is not merged; merging follows review. This follows John's ruling of 8 Nov: build the call-layer fix now, and settle the budget rule with the live replay at review.

### What landed

- **Whole or loud.** `streamChat` and `streamChatWithTools` now hold the reply until `finish_reason` is `stop` or `tool_calls`.
  - A `length` stop is retried once with a larger budget.
  - If the reply still isn't whole, the call throws `TruncatedOutputError`. No `done` event fires and nothing is cached.
  - Routes answer **502 `OUTPUT_TRUNCATED`** and name the model, the reason and the hidden-reasoning tokens.
  - This covers brief, recap, the run and session summaries, run-paragraph, feedback-title, scan, scan-retire, observer-pass and roadmap-orientation.
  - The callers that stream to a person and handle a cut-off themselves pass `allowPartial` and keep today's behaviour: roadmap layers and chat, Ship's Biscuit, and task chat and Flight Companion.
- **Budget from the catalog** (`lib/call-budget.js`).
  - Any model the catalog lists as able to reason gets prose plus headroom, kept within `max_completion_tokens` and the context left.
  - The first attempt sends no `reasoning` field. The retry bounds reasoning explicitly only when hidden reasoning ate the cap.
- **The catalog normalizer now matches the live `/models` shape**, pinned as a fixture: `default_enabled` is three-valued (true, false or absent), and efforts and limits are kept.
- **`scripts/replay-brief.mjs`** is the review check. It replays snapshot `82b963e0` (LIN-4352, 14:13:25 UTC) twice:
  - once as the 7 Nov request byte for byte, which settles why Haiku stopped;
  - once through today's layer, which shows whether the budget rule holds.

### Evidence

- **New witnesses:** 20 tests. 17 fail on the old code. The 3 that pass are the standalone budget checks and the guard that a whole first-hop answer still short-circuits.
- **Local runs:** `npm run test:unit` passes 24,344 of 24,344 (main was 24,324). `test:hermetic:keyed` passes 24,344 with zero non-loopback sockets. Secret scan passes.
- **Replay script:** checked against a fake OpenRouter. The requests went out as 3000 (bare), then 6000 with no reasoning field, then 6000 with `reasoning.max_tokens` 3000, and the brief came out whole.

### Not done here

- **The live replay on Haiku 5.5.** There's no key in the worker. That's the reviewer's check, per the ruling.
- **The hand lists.** `REASONING_MODEL_PREFIXES` stays, with its reason written beside it: the catalog says gpt-5.4-mini doesn't reason by default, but it measurably does. `MODEL_PRICING`, `AVAILABLE_MODELS` and the suggestion lists are the next piece. `FREE_TIER_MODEL_IDS` waits on the free-tier ruling.

## Review — LIN-4358

PR [#2362](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2362), head `ef36e771`. This is the call-layer piece only, built under John's 8 Nov ruling ("build the call-layer fix now; settle the budget rule with the live replay at review").

CI: green on `ef36e771`. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4 and the secret scan all pass, and so does the `CI success` rollup.

**Summary.** The call-layer change is correct and well witnessed. **The live replay that John put at review has not run.** This worker has no OpenRouter key, and the proxy does not expose raw call-log rows: `/issues/LIN-4352/cost` gives only per-feature totals. So the budget rule is still unsettled, and that is the first ledger item.
